surfaces.userScenario: A Runner advertises support for a one-turn diagnostic so a subscription model test runs on the right computer without creating a task.
Nothing to set: the Runner sets it on a task step whose agent runs under its own home folder, so git and gh there still use your sign-in.
Click a filename in a reply to open it on the Runner that wrote it. Cairn shows a clear unavailable notice when that Runner cannot preview files.
Nothing to set: each Runner reports whether its GitHub sign-in can push to the team's GitHub repositories, so a task waits with a clear login hint instead of failing after an hour of work.
Nothing to set: a Mac Runner reports when its Android phone support is ready, so Settings can offer pairing without asking you to install platform-tools yourself.
Nothing to set: a Runner reports the Android phones it can currently see, so Settings shows their real state and the Coordinator can use only a phone you paired.

Open Settings, Computers, and choose Add Android phone on a local Mac runner; with the phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi, enter the pairing endpoint and code the phone shows, consent once, and the phone becomes available to the Coordinator.
Nothing to set: pressing Stop on your own message that has not started sends its id, so that turn is the one stopped.

A new desktop user does nothing: while the Runner is working the computer stays awake but its screen may sleep; the menu-bar menu can instead keep the screen on or, on AC-powered macOS, keep running with the lid closed.
A new Mac user never sets it: the app hands its bundled browser driver to its own runner so the Coordinator can open pages.
A new Mac user never sets or sees it: the runner tells its own browser launcher which browser to start for each page the Coordinator opens.
Nothing to set: when you have two or more computers, choosing one in the new-task row sends its id so the task waits for that computer.
Set in Docker or hosted cloud deployments to enable continuous SQLite WAL replication and cold-volume restore to an S3-compatible bucket; leave unset to run Node directly with zero overhead.
Optional relative S3 key prefix for Litestream WAL replication inside the bucket (defaults to server.db); unset on a single-user self-hosted bucket.
Optional S3-compatible endpoint URL (such as R2, Tigris, GCS interop, or MinIO) paired with CAIRN_LITESTREAM_BUCKET when not targeting AWS S3 directly.
Optional bucket region for Litestream S3 replication; defaults to auto when CAIRN_LITESTREAM_ENDPOINT is set.
Nothing to set: creating a schedule inside a Coordinator conversation records that thread id so recurring requests fire directly in chat instead of opening a separate task.

Nothing to set: passed internally by the Runner supervisor to the child Runner process so it starts directly instead of nesting another update supervisor.
Nothing to set: passed internally by the Runner supervisor to track one probation boot attempt and confirm or roll back a Runner update.
Nothing to set: passed internally by the Runner supervisor so the spawned Runner slot knows which release version it is verifying.
Nothing to set: optional release version override read by a standalone Runner when its bundled build version metadata is overridden by packaging or tests.
Nothing to set: set when Cairn Desktop starts its bundled Runner so standalone Runner self-update stays off inside the Mac app bundle.
Nothing to set: set inside Cairn container images so containerized Runners report manual container-image updates instead of attempting in-place self-updates.
Nothing to set: optional read-only install flag instructing a Runner to show the manual update notice instead of downloading updates.
Nothing to set: used only in automated tests and isolated verification to allow a standalone Runner script to self-update into its test slot.
Nothing to set: set automatically when you rotate an offline Runner's token so its row in Settings -> Runners shows the one reconnect command until that computer reconnects.
Nothing to set: holds the hashed replacement Runner token in SQLite during an online token rotation so a server restart between claim and ack recovers cleanly without split-brain credentials.
